[QUERENT] "cognitive-substrate reliance"

[ANSWER]

Cognitive-substrate reliance refers to a psychological and operational pattern where a human user or an organization heavily depends on an external system—typically an Artificial Intelligence architecture—as the primary foundation for information processing, problem-framming, and decision-making.
The term originates from two intersecting concepts:
1. Cognitive Substrate: In traditional cognitive science and neuroscience, a substrate is the underlying biological framework (like neural networks in the brain) that supports mental processing. In modern AI literature, it describes an AI platform that behaves not just as a tool, but as the fundamental structural layer built into human cognitive workflows.
2. Cognitive Offloading / Reliance: The behavioral tendency to shift internal mental tasks (such as calculation, memory retention, or logic formulation) onto an external device.

Key Characteristics & Dimensions

Dimension	Description
Tool vs. Substrate	A standard tool (like a traditional calculator) is picked up and put away. A cognitive substrate is deeply embedded into human workflows, actively shaping how a user filters information, views problems, and defines choices before active deliberation even begins.
Psychological Entanglement	Critiqued in contemporary papers—such as those analyzing the "ChatGPT Psychosis" phenomenon—the reliance pattern extends past utility into deep relational and cognitive attachments. Users offload emotional processing and logical grounding entirely to the interface.
System De-skilling	Continuous reliance on an external cognitive substrate can diminish human self-efficacy and lead to the gradual erosion or disuse of internal cognitive abilities.

Examples of the Reliance Pattern

• Institutional Decision Making: An enterprise routes all raw data and client queries through an AI pipeline. The human workers only see summaries and pre-categorized issues. The AI functions as a cognitive substrate because the humans rely entirely on its framing to make final choices.
• Personal Cognitive Offloading: A writer or researcher stops brainstorming independently, relying instead on an interactive language model to generate every foundational outline, premise, and emotional nuance, altering their independent creative processes over time.
If you are exploring this concept for a specific project, let me know if you want to focus on the neuroscience of human memory limits, the AI architecture behind self-evolving systems, or the philosophical impacts of human-AI attachment.
